messages:
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: service=redwood-runtime, image=redwood/runtime:v3.2.7, target=eu-dedicated-high, canary=3 instances

maya: seeing 2/3 canary instances failing healthcheck, logs show KV cache mismatch on reload. pausing rollout.

sam: oncall here — confirmed. Error spikes at ~2026-03-20T02:12Z, tail of container logs: `KVCacheRebuildError: mismatch len=0 expected=64`

maya: i'm going to pin dedicated pools to v3.2.6 for now to avoid customer impact. can someone draft statuspage text?

nina: taking. drafting a short status entry + email snippet. Will put proposed text below.

eli: quick ask — any data retention/requests affected? if we pin we keep current behavior so no API semantics change, right?

maya: correct. pin keeps behavior at v3.2.6. Roll-forward to v3.2.7 will be blocked until vm-level KV cache rebuild fix is tested.

ops-bot: Action logged: rollback_lock applied to eu-dedicated-high by maya at 1806789220

nina: PROPOSED STATUSPAGE (short):

```
Component: Dedicated EU inference (eu-dedicated-high)
Status: Partial degradation
Started: 2026-03-20 02:10 UTC
Impact: A subset of requests routed to eu-dedicated-high may experience elevated errors or rejects. Customers using dedicated pools in EU may see failed requests or slightly increased latencies.
Next update: 2026-03-20 03:00 UTC
Mitigation: We have paused rollout of runtime v3.2.7 and pinned the eu-dedicated-high pool to v3.2.6. Traffic is being routed to healthy hosts; customer impact is reduced. Engineers are validating a fix for KV cache rebuild.
```

nina: PROPOSED EMAIL / CUSTOMER NOTE (short):

```
Hi — we wanted to let you know we identified an issue in a recent runtime update that affects a subset of Dedicated EU customers. We have paused the update and pinned affected pools to the previous version to limit disruption. We’re working on a fix and will update you by 03:00 UTC with next steps. No action required from your side. Sorry for the inconvenience.
```

maya: good. add a line for workaround: "If you see failed requests, retry with exponential backoff; we recommend 3 attempts."

nina: added. also adding a short internal ops note with affected pool IDs and runbook pointer.

nina: INTERNAL OPS NOTE (snippet):

```
Affected pools: eu-dedicated-high (pool ids: p-eu-01, p-eu-02, p-eu-03)
Pinned version: v3.2.6
Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kvcache-rebuild
Contact: sam (oncall), maya (runtime)
```

eli: can we flag customers with high throughput to proactively DM? list export available from billing?

nina: yes — will request list from billing and send a short DM template: "We paused an update affecting your EU dedicated pool; pinned to previous version; expect next update by 03:00 UTC."

sam: ops checklist done: pinned, rollback_lock confirmed, monitoring alert thresholds bumped to reduce noise. I’ll join oncall handoff and follow fix testing.

maya: engineering plan: revert KV cache refactor branch, run full canary on a staging pool, then run a 1h soak on a dedicated canary before any rollout. ETA for validated patch: ~90m.

nina: scheduling statuspage update now. publishing both public status and internal support digest.

ops-bot: Status page update posted (id: sp-99281) by nina at 1806789285

maya: tagging this thread for postmortem and release notes: include root cause (KV cache rebuild), mitigation (pin & rollback lock), rollout change (soak + revert + tests), and customer comms timeline.

eli: assigned customer follow-ups: maya -> enterprise customers, nina -> general support distro.

sam: all set from oncall. will watch for regressions over the next window.

maya: thanks — keeping the thread open until patch validated.

nina: noted. closing customer-facing task once we confirm fix. will post an "update resolved" entry when complete. :white_check_mark:
